Ava — did the quick microbench and a short writeup attached (microbench-results.csv). High level findings: 
- Baseline tokens per logical call (no prefill, cache hit 25%, mean batch 4): 630 tokens/call on average -> tokens/$ = ~1,900 calls per $1M (hosted pricing X used = $0.53 per 1k tokens; adjust if finance updates).
- No-caching scenario increases tokens/call ~22% (median) because of repeated prefix tokens; tokens/$ drops to ~1,550 calls per $1M.
- Prefill scenario (+512 tokens on 30% calls) adds ~150 tokens/call across dataset -> latency impact modest (p95 increases by ~8%); batching partly amortizes CPU cost.
- Batching sensitivity: mean batch 2 increases latency p95 by ~40ms but reduces tokens/$ by ~8% compared to mean batch 4; spike windows (50 rps) produce smaller batches — we recommend conservative rollout with batch mean target 2 and opportunistic increase to 4 once traffic stabilizes.

Recommendation for MAP: include two cost rows (Conservative: cache disabled, batch mean 2; Optimistic: cache enabled 25%, batch mean 4) and a short acceptance test that runs 10k calls with your traffic mix and verifies token consumption within +/-10% of the model.

Irene — I left a note on the microbench sheet about cases where PHI restrictions will force cache off (repeatability requirements + audit), happy to sync if you want deeper numbers.

Ben
